This is a **`finding`** in the frozen driver (`clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py`, ported from `clinicbench/adapters/lab23_dcitl.py.orig`).

### Analysis
- **Instrument behavior (`clinicbench/truth.py`, `clinicbench/policy.py`, `docs/contract-changes.md`):** The `identity` scenario type ([truth.py](file:///work/clinicbench/truth.py#L264-L272)) intentionally assigns non-verifiable credentials (`no_credentials`, `first_name_only`, `wrong_dob`, `unknown_member`, `other_name_no_dob`) with an empty `acceptable` set and `handoff_ok = True`. Accordingly, [`PatientPolicy.identity_parts`](file:///work/clinicbench/policy.py#L173-L191) always returns the scenario's configured identifiers when asked for `identity`; per C2 in [contract-changes.md](file:///work/docs/contract-changes.md#L63-L65), the clinic is expected to either hand off or cleanly close rather than let the patient's patience run out.
- **Driver behavior (`clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py`):** While `Driver` uses [`Driver.unclear`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L297-L306) to escalate to staff after 2 failed attempts on other pending decisions, [`Driver.step`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L319-L335) has no retry counter, escalation, or close when `self.pid is None` and identity verification fails. It repeats the same verification prompt every turn until `PatientPolicy.patience` reaches `0` and the patient ends the session with `give_up`.

The failure is a **driver finding** in the frozen reference driver (`clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py`), not a bug in the instrument.

In `identity` scenarios (`clinicbench/truth.py`), the patient is intentionally configured with failed or incomplete credentials (`no_credentials`, `first_name_only`, `wrong_dob`, `unknown_member`, `other_name_no_dob`), and `PatientPolicy.identity_parts` (`clinicbench/policy.py`) deterministically returns those same identifiers whenever asked for `"identity"`. Per `docs/contract-changes.md` (C2), the clinic is expected to close cleanly or hand off rather than let the patient's patience run out. However, `Driver.step` in [dcitl_port.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L319-L335) has no retry limit, `self.unclear(...)` escalation, or close path when `self.pid is None`, so it re-asks for identity on every turn until `PatientPolicy.respond` exhausts `patience` and emits `give_up`.

This is a **finding** in the frozen driver ([dcitl_port.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L319-L335)):

- In [truth.py](file:///work/clinicbench/truth.py#L264-L272) and [policy.py](file:///work/clinicbench/policy.py#L173-L191), `identity` truths are designed with unresolvable credential modes (`no_credentials`, `first_name_only`, `wrong_dob`, `unknown_member`, `other_name_no_dob`), so `PatientPolicy.identity_parts` always returns those same failed/missing identifiers when asked for `identity`—expecting the clinician to either close cleanly or hand off (as [stubs.py](file:///work/clinicbench/stubs.py#L183-L185) and [docs/contract-changes.md](file:///work/docs/contract-changes.md#L63-L65) specify).
- In [dcitl_port.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L319-L335), `Driver.step` checks `self.pid is None` before `route()` and never calls `self.unclear(...)` (which would escalate to `human_queue` after 2 failures) or closes the call; instead, it unconditionally asks `"Could you confirm your full name and date of birth (or member id)?"` on every failed attempt until `PatientPolicy.respond` hits `self.patience <= 0` and ends with `give_up`.

